Basis of Recommendation

The client currently holds Northstar WholeLife Secure with death/TPD cover of S$180,000, critical illness cover of S$60,000, annual premium of S$3,600, and lifetime coverage. The proposed replacement is Harbor EliteTerm with death/TPD cover of S$500,000, critical illness cover of S$200,000, annual premium of S$1,850, and coverage to age 70.

After discussing the pros and cons of whole life, term life and investment-linked plans, the client preferred Harbor EliteTerm because it provides materially higher protection to age 70 at a lower premium.

The client requires adequate protection for death/TPD and critical illness, with coverage to age 70. Compared to the existing policy, the proposed plan provides higher death/TPD cover, higher critical illness cover, and longer-term protection while reducing the annual premium.

Total annual premiums do not exceed 50% of the client's surplus.

The client was informed that in the event of non-disclosure of any pre-existing medical conditions, the insurer has the right to not pay out benefits as stated if diagnosed due to pre-existing conditions.
The product was recommended after fact-find, needs analysis, and product comparison.
The client is aware that the Financial Consultant may receive additional commission for selling the recommended product.
The client has agreed for soft copies of the documents to be electronically mailed after the company has processed them.

1. May incur penalties / transaction costs for terminating the existing policy(ies) or investment product(s), without gaining any real benefit from replacing them.
2. Financial benefits accumulated over the years may be lost.
3. May be offered a lower level of benefit at a higher or same cost (or the same benefit at higher cost); the new policy may be less suitable.
4. If existing medical conditions are covered by the existing plan, coverage for those conditions may be lost.

The client was advised of the replacement disadvantages and wishes to proceed.
Other available options—such as increasing the sum assured under the existing policy, attaching riders, or converting the policy—have been explored. The recommendation to proceed with a replacement was made only after a thorough assessment confirmed that it is suitable and in the best interest of the client.
